fields.why: The health-outcome quantities (23/26 ill, symptom percentages, median onset) are all one-group summaries. B's 'comparison' rests on pool logs showing 'two compliant free chlorine concentration readings, not the expected 15', a compliance count against a target, which is defensible under the literal fixed-referent wording but is an inspection finding, not an outcome claim (as A's review note says).

The SNP analysis showing the two isolates were 'highly related with a two-SNP difference' is a laboratory method that supports a common exposure; the brief excludes lab methods unless they produce or qualify the analyzed quantity, so it is not an 'other' procedure.

Follows analytic_depth: the only fixed-referent contrast is chlorine-log compliance (2 vs 15 expected readings), not a health outcome. Rule needed: whether comparisons of environmental or process measures (inspection compliance) count, given that data_focus is defined by public health outcomes.

'Maine CDC used illness reports to identify six households' uses the reports only for case finding; the analyzed data are the household interviews and questionnaires (and pool logs). The brief says not to list sources used only to build a roster.

brief_issues: The brief should say whether analytic_depth and comparison cover non-outcome measures such as inspection or compliance counts against a code requirement in an outbreak report.
